changes_vs_current: New topic. Averaged four people sources: worldwide sales (35 entries, missing 40), pageviews (~33 entries, missing 38), Ranker top 10 and PixlParade top 10 (missing 15). Raw order: PS2 2.0, Switch 2.75, PS4 5.25, PS1 7.5, X360 8.0, SNES 9.25, PS3 9.5, PS5 9.75, Game Boy 10.5, DS 10.75, Wii 11.0, N64 11.25, NES 11.25, Switch 2 13.25, GameCube 13.5, PSP 13.75, Series X 14.0, Xbox One 14.75, GBA 15.0, 3DS ~16.75, Genesis 17.25, Xbox 18.5, Atari 2600 19.0, Wii U 19.75, Vita ~20, Dreamcast 20.75, Saturn 21.25. Gut-check moves: Wii 11 to 3 (gut top-3, #1 most played in YouGov UK, 45% favorite Nintendo console, ~101M sold; only the enthusiast votes leave it out); NES 13 to 8 and N64 12 to 9 (gut picks; Ranker #5 and #3; N64 the most-used classic console in the US Solitaired survey); PS3 7 to 12 and DS 10 to 13 to make room (not gut picks; each rests mostly on one strong signal); Atari 2600 23 to 16 (gut pick; sales #20 and pageviews #26 keep it outside the top 12). Bare 'Nintendo' and 'Sega' are not aliases (brand names). Game Boy Color is an alias of Game Boy, matching the combined sales line.
confidence: Medium. PS2 and Switch at 1-2 are solid. Positions 3-13 are a tight cluster whose order is partly judgment; no representative US all-time favorite-console poll was found, and the two votes are enthusiast audiences (the top 10 is still backed by sales and pageviews). US-only sales were not available as a full list (Circana: DS #1, Switch #2, PS2 #3 in the US), which could justify a higher DS. Pageviews favor current hardware. Near misses: Dreamcast, PS Vita, Sega Saturn, Steam Deck, Master System, Atari Jaguar.
